```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)
opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

### This is how one can add a figure:
# ```{r FIGLABEL, out.width = "100%", fig.cap="CAPTION", echo=FALSE}
# plot(1:5)
# ### Or from file:
# include_graphics(path = "./FILENAME.PNG")
# ```
#
# Crossref: \@ref(fig:FIGLABEL)


### For tables use kable function:
# ```{r TABLABEL, echo=FALSE}
# kable(head(iris),
#   caption = "CAPTION")
# ```
#
# Crossref: \@ref(tab:TABLABEL)
```


# First section

This is another example of using RMarkdown. Lets look at the following analysis:

```{r}
lmfit <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Species, data = iris)
summary(lmfit)
```

## Results in a table

We want to show the results in a table. We can print R data frames (or matrices) as tables:

```{r coeftable, echo=FALSE}
### Get the coefficients as table:
sumy <- summary(lmfit)
coeftbl <- sumy$coefficients
coeftbl <- apply(coeftbl, 2, round, digits=2)
kable(coeftbl, caption = 'Results of my linear model.')
```

As you can see in Table \@ref(tab:coeftable), the results show...


## Adding a figure

Figure \@ref(fig:boxplot) shows a boxplot of the iris data.

```{r boxplot, out.width = "100%", fig.cap="iris data boxplot.", echo=FALSE}
### Look at data:
boxplot(Sepal.Length ~ Species, data = iris)
```

# Adding a figure from a file

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
### Create figure file:
jpeg(filename = './boxplot.jpeg', width = 10, height = 10, units = 'cm', 
     pointsize = 10, res = 300)
boxplot(Sepal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, col='blue')
dev.off()
```


```{r boxplotfile, out.width = "100%", fig.cap="Again an iris boxplot.", echo=FALSE}
### Insert file:
include_graphics(path = "./boxplot.jpeg")
```

This is Figure \@ref(fig:boxplotfile).
